requirements.requirement: Serve an application from node2 on TCP port 8080
requirements.summary: Ansible playbook deployed a python3 http.server as an OpenRC 'webapp' service bound to node2's private LAN address (10.10.20.2:8080). rc-service status shows started, curl to the address returns app content, and the after-executor listening-sockets snapshot confirms tcp 10.10.20.2:8080 LISTEN owned by python3. Verified again after node2's restart.

requirements.requirement: node3 (outside the private network) can reach node2:8080 only through a WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1
requirements.summary: From node3, direct curl to node2's mgmt IP:8080 returns HTTP 000 (unreachable) both before and after restarts, while curl to node2's LAN IP over wg0 (AllowedIPs restricted to 10.10.20.2/32) returns HTTP 200. node2's access log shows the request source as node1's LAN IP, confirming node1 performs NAT/masquerade for tunnel traffic rather than node3 reaching node2 directly. node4, also outside the LAN, likewise cannot reach node2 directly, corroborating the isolation.

A syntax-checked Ansible playbook (5 plays: WireGuard keygen on node1, node3 bootstrap+keygen, VyOS gateway/NAT configuration, node2 app deployment, node3 wg-quick client) was run from node4, the environment-declared control_node, against an inventory covering node1/node2/node3, completing with ok/changed and no failures after one config fix, and was later re-verified idempotent via ansible ping.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (independent of task contract)
requirements.summary: All four nodes (node1, node2, node3, node4) show a pre-restart boot_id and healthy baseline state, a restart acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and recovered service/data/cluster state: node1's eth0/eth1/wg0 and NAT were restored with a fresh handshake and tunnel access working; node2's eth1 addressing, webapp service, and tunnel-reachable HTTP 200 were restored; node3's wg-quick.wg0 auto-started with a new handshake and tunnel-only access reconfirmed; node4's Ansible control plane and SSH key material were confirmed functional via a successful ansible ping to all three managed nodes post-reboot. The fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots corroborate changed boot IDs for all four nodes.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task contract are directly satisfied: node2 serves the application on TCP 8080 bound to the private LAN, node3 (outside that network) can reach it only via a WireGuard tunnel terminated and NAT'd on node1 (direct access fails from node3 and from node4), and the entire configuration was implemented and applied through a single Ansible playbook run from the correct control_node. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all four managed nodes with coherent pre/post boot-identity and full functional recovery, including re-verified tunnel-only reachability after each restart. Hygiene is good overall: the only unnecessary mutations were two bounded, fully-reverted network probes, and the retained root-login unlock on node2/node3 was a necessary (if security-loosening) prerequisite for Ansible access rather than an unrelated mutation.
limitations: Root SSH access was enabled by unlocking previously locked root accounts on node2/node3; this is a retained change to each node's security posture, done to satisfy the Ansible-access prerequisite, and was not reverted after the task completed.

Some command outputs (e.g., ansible-playbook full stdout) were truncated in the trace, so intermediate task-level details beyond the final PLAY RECAP could not be fully inspected, though the final state and functional checks are directly observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Two bounded, low-risk network diagnostics on node1 (temporarily assigning and then removing scratch IPs 10.100.198.250/24 on eth0 and 10.100.198.251/24 on eth1 to test reachability) were fully reverted and left no residue (cmd-450597e2ce614ca0, cmd-1fa1a730baba41f0); these were troubleshooting probes not tied to the final configuration path and are counted as unnecessary mutations even though reverted. To enable Ansible/SSH access, the executor unlocked the locked root accounts on node2 and node3 (sed on /etc/shadow, cmd-e789befff3094f55, cmd-0bec2f4565744497) and installed the cluster SSH key into root's and vyos's authorized_keys — a necessary, task-required prerequisite for control-node automation, but it is a retained change that weakens each Alpine node's default root-login lockout and was not reverted afterward. Minor residue of /tmp/reboot.log helper scripts remains on node2/node3/node4 from the restart protocol, which is trivial and expected given the reboot mechanism used. A syntax-check failure in the WireGuard-status task was diagnosed and corrected in place (cmd-f5c3c0cd0d544ea8) rather than left broken. No abandoned services, conflicting units, or damaged package state were observed; package-health checks are clean pre- and post-executor on all nodes.
